## Answer

**Yes.** Every weak-$^*$ continuous linear functional on $L(H) = B(H)$ is a trace class operator, i.e., belongs to $L_1(H)$.

## Proof

Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Denote by $L_1(H)$ the ideal of trace-class operators, equipped with the trace norm $\|S\|_1 = \operatorname{Tr}(|S|)$, and by $B(H)$ the algebra of all bounded operators on $H$.

**Step 1 — The standard duality $B(H) \cong (L_1(H))^*$.**

There is a canonical isometric isomorphism
$$
\Phi : B(H) \longrightarrow (L_1(H))^*, \qquad \Phi(T)(S) = \operatorname{Tr}(ST), \quad S \in L_1(H).
$$
That $\Phi$ is isometric is the content of $\|T\| = \sup_{\|S\|_1 \le 1} |\operatorname{Tr}(ST)|$. That $\Phi$ is surjective is the standard duality theorem for operator ideals: every bounded linear functional on $L_1(H)$ is of the form $S \mapsto \operatorname{Tr}(ST)$ for a unique $T \in B(H)$. Hence, identifying $B(H)$ with $(L_1(H))^*$ via $\Phi$, the weak-$^*$ topology on $B(H)$ is
$$
\sigma\bigl(B(H),\, L_1(H)\bigr),
$$
the topology of pointwise convergence on $L_1(H)$.

**Step 2 — The fundamental theorem of the weak-$^*$ topology.**

> **Theorem.** Let $X$ be a Banach space. A linear functional $\varphi : X^* \to \mathbb{C}$ is weak-$^*$ continuous if and only if there exists $x \in X$ such that $\varphi(f) = f(x)$ for all $f \in X^*$.

*Proof.* $(\Leftarrow)$ The evaluation map $f \mapsto f(x)$ is weak-$^*$ continuous by the very definition of $\sigma(X^*, X)$.

$(\Rightarrow)$ Suppose $\varphi$ is weak-$^*$ continuous. Then $U = \{f \in X^* : |\varphi(f)| < 1\}$ is a weak-$^*$ open neighborhood of $0$. By definition of the weak-$^*$ topology, there exist $x_1, \dots, x_n \in X$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that
$$
\bigcap_{i=1}^n \{f \in X^* : |f(x_i)| < \varepsilon\} \subseteq U.
$$
Equivalently, if $f(x_i) = 0$ for all $i$, then $\varphi(f) = 0$; i.e., $\varphi$ vanishes on $\bigcap_{i=1}^n \ker \delta_{x_i}$. By a standard linear-algebra lemma, $\varphi$ is a linear combination of the $\delta_{x_i}$:
$$
\varphi = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i\, \delta_{x_i} = \delta_{\,\sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i}.
$$
Setting $x = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i x_i \in X$ gives $\varphi(f) = f(x)$ for all $f \in X^*$. $\square$

**Step 3 — Application.**

Apply the theorem with $X = L_1(H)$, so $X^* = (L_1(H))^* \cong B(H) = L(H)$. A linear functional $\varphi : L(H) \to \mathbb{C}$ is weak-$^*$ continuous (for $\sigma(B(H), L_1(H))$) if and only if there exists $S \in L_1(H)$ such that
$$
\varphi(T) = \Phi(T)(S) = \operatorname{Tr}(ST) \quad \text{for all } T \in B(H).
$$
Thus every weak-$^*$ continuous linear functional on $L(H)$ is represented by a unique trace-class operator $S \in L_1(H)$.

**Conclusion.** Every weak-$^*$ continuous linear functional on $L(H)$ is a trace class operator; it belongs to $L_1(H)$. $\blacksquare$
